calls.head: There’s no curse: Skinner vs. The Stars
calls.body: Skinner has been shaky against the Stars since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
calls.call: If Skinner starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .899 than to his .850 against the Stars.

calls.body: The Jets’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Stars’ power play is the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Jets tonight.

calls.head: Picky vs. Trigger-happy
calls.body: The Stars wait for good looks, but the Jets settle for hopeful ones. Dallas is near the top of the league for shot quality, and Winnipeg is one of the worst. The more dangerous chances should be the Stars’.
calls.call: The Stars’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Jets’.

surprises.head: Winnipeg found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Winnipeg usually gets some of the league’s least dangerous shots. Not tonight: a 9.1% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 5.9% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: A rough night for Jake Oettinger
surprises.body: Oettinger allowed 6 goals on 27 shots, worth 3.2 expected goals: 2.8 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 25 starts.

story.head: Scheifele ties Hawerchuk for the Jets’ points record
paras: Arttu Hyry got the scoring started for the Stars early in the first. The Jets’ Dylan DeMelo left in the first period and didn’t return. The next day, he was placed on injured reserve. Winnipeg had a goal taken off for offside late in the period, but it didn’t cost them in the end. Roope Hintz made it 2-0 for the Stars later in the period. There were six goals in the second period alone. Dylan Samberg got the Jets on the board early in the period, and Mark Scheifele tied it 2-2 later in the period. David Perron scored his first goal for Dallas a little over four minutes later to put the Stars back ahead 3-2. Dawson Mercer scored twice and Scheifele once in just under six minutes later in the period to turn a 3-2 deficit into a 5-3 lead. The third period belonged to the Jets: Kyle Connor scored, Gabriel Vilardi scored, and Cole Koepke scored to make it 8-3. Dallas pulled Jake Oettinger after six goals and turned to Casey DeSmith for the rest of the third. Three players had three-point nights: Connor with a goal and two assists, Vilardi with a goal and two assists, and Scheifele with two goals and an assist.

Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Stuart Skinner made 30 saves for the Jets. The Jets moved to 9-8-3, sixth in the Central, while the Stars fell to 10-6-2, fourth in the Central.

items.text: Mark Scheifele tied Dale Hawerchuk for first on the Jets’ all-time scoring list, with 929 points.
